entries.heading: **Emerging Scholars Research Fellow**, Early Modern Sikh History. Mentor: Satnam Singh, Harvard Sikh Center

bullets.text: *Dissemination and the making of Khalsa authority in a contested panth*: examining how the Khalsa asserted dominance over the wider Sikh world within decades of its founding, against rival claimants including the Bandai Khalsa, Minas, and Ram Raiyas

Arguing that the consolidation of “authentic Sikh teachings” through katha was instrumental to that dominance; working from Gurmukhi and Persian primary sources, including works attributed to Bhai Mani Singh, hukamname, and rahit-nama literature

entries.heading: Undergraduate Researcher, **Digital History & Urban Studies**. PI: Dr. Louis Hamilton, NJIT

bullets.text: Digital mapping of how religious institutions shaped urban form in medieval and early modern Italy; field research conducted in Rome and Florence

[*Power vs. the People*](https://uploads.knightlab.com/storymapjs/cbb86fd8d8b9cdc53b4e6e879d9db5f6/rome-2026/index.html) (HIST 328; 18 sites): layered Counter-Reformation Marian shrines against Julius II’s 1508 papal axis on the Via Giulia

[*Processions and Power*](https://uploads.knightlab.com/storymapjs/cbb86fd8d8b9cdc53b4e6e879d9db5f6/final-essay-draft/index.html) (HIST 329; 22 sites): traced how Florence’s expansion turned liturgical processions into contested displays of ecclesiastical and household prestige
